# Synthetic fsite/v0.5.3 email access fixture

`state.tar.gz` is generated by the actual old implementation at monorepo commit
`662f837ed5875de4cbf55acd1d1adfe288e762a1` (`fsite/v0.5.3`), not by candidate
schema declarations. It contains one synthetic published shared Site, one
publisher-email principal, one email share, one blob, the stable IDs, and one
old viewer cookie. All identities and key material are public test data. There
is no production data or production secret. The old writer closes its SQLite
connection before archiving.

`generate.rs` is an integration test for the **old** `finitesites-engine` crate.
To regenerate, use a scratch worktree at the exact commit, copy this file into
`finite-sites/crates/finitesites-engine/tests/legacy_email_fixture.rs`, then run
in that worktree's pinned environment:

```sh
SITES_LEGACY_FIXTURE_OUTPUT=/private/tmp/sites-legacy-email-fixture \
  nix develop . -c cargo test --locked -p finitesites-engine \
    --test legacy_email_fixture
```

The output directory must not already exist. Archive its contents as
`state.tar.gz` (registry, blobs, and three metadata text files). IDs and cookie
bytes can differ on regeneration; the companion metadata pins the old values.
Do not replace the old writer with SQL or the candidate implementation.

`legacy_email_access.rs` unpacks into a fresh temporary directory and opens the
old state with the candidate. It proves content, IDs, active version, visibility,
publisher and allowlisted email access, denied email access, old-cookie decoding,
new-domain email cookie minting, and durable revocation after reopening. It does
not prove browser navigation, WorkOS, a production migration, Git Repository
migration, or cookies being sent across domains. Those are separate cutover gates.
